To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fluid inertia significantly affects the behavior of a three-dimensional airway-reopening problem, and that this effect is captured by a single material parameter, ReCa.
fluid inertia causes a substantial increase in the pressure needed to drive the air-finger at a given speed and that this pressure increase scales as the square of the Reynolds number.
the pressure required to propagate the air finger at the same speed is significantly increased by fluid inertia, and that the increase is larger when the air finger is longer.
